data.long_meaning: Bhausaheb is a compound name derived from two Sanskrit words: Bhau (Bhauma or Bhagavan, meaning 'Lord of the Earth') and Saheb (Swami or Master). The name evokes the image of a powerful and prosperous leader, revered and respected by all. The name Bhausaheb carries the meaning “Lord of Wealth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhausaheb usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of wealth and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Bhausaheb is a name of great prestige and honor in Hindu culture. It is often given to boys born into families that have a deep connection to their land and community. The name signifies strength, leadership, and the blessing of Lord Bhauma, the deity representing the power and fertility of the Earth. Bhausahebs are respected figures in their communities, and they carry the responsibilities of providing for their families and protecting their people. This name has an enduring legacy, passed down through generations, and it continues to inspire a sense of pride and tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Bhausaheb not only invokes a sense of earthly power but also signifies a spiritual connection with the divine. Bhau, as a reference to Lord Bhauma, signifies that the bearer of this name is protected and blessed by the divine power of nature. Saheb, meaning Swami or Master, signifies the bearer of this name is not only a servant of the divine but also a leader in the path of spiritual growth. Thus, the name Bhausaheb carries a deep spiritual significance, representing both a strong connection to the earthly world and a commitment to the path of spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Bhausaheb was a Maratha military leader and poet who served under Chhatrapati Shahuji Maharaj during the late 17th and early 18th century. He is best known for his military victories, including the battle of Wadgaon and the Battle of Pavan Khind, which secured the Maratha Empire's position in the Deccan region.

Bhausaheb was also a celebrated poet and wrote many compositions in Marathi and Sanskrit languages. He is especially known for his work 'Gangasahasra', which is a collection of 1000 verses on the Goddess Ganga. This work exemplifies the rich literary heritage of the Maratha court.
